transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining it. But I know what's going on. My wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. Look, my tools don’t move themselves. I know exactly where I leave them. And my fishing plans don’t just get spoiled by accident every single weekend. It's been happening for a while now, and after all these months, I can see plain as day that he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. They wanted me to come talk to you about it, but that's the truth of what's happening.

Over the past several months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or low energy, or on the other hand, unusually elated, energetic, or needing very little sleep?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean... I'm not depressed or sad, and I'm definitely not bouncing off the walls with a bunch of extra energy or anything. I sleep normal. I just get up, go to my shift at the plant, and come home. 

I guess I'm just frustrated, you know? It's aggravating having someone mess with your things and having people tell you it's not happening. But as far as my mood goes... no, it's just regular. I don't have any of those other things you mentioned.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to hear or see?

No, I haven't. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there. I know what you're getting at, but my mind is fine. I just see what's actually happening in my own house. Like I said, my tools get moved and things get messed with, but I'm not hallucinating it. So no, no voices or anything like that.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions, or used alcohol or drugs, that started around the same time these suspicions began?

No, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or had any seizures or... anything medical. My health is fine, honestly. I don't take drugs, and I might have a beer if I'm watching a game, but I don't really drink much. So no, nothing like that. Like I keep saying, there's nothing wrong with me physically or mentally. I'm just a regular guy dealing with someone coming into my house and messing with my things.
Aside from this situation with your wife's relative, has your ability to function—like performing well at your job, taking care of yourself, or getting along with others—changed at all recently?

No, not at all. I mean, like I said, I still get up every day, go to my shift at the plant, do my assembler work, and come home. I keep the bills paid. I take care of myself the exact same way I always have. My job is fine, and I get along with the guys at work just fine. 

The only trouble I'm having is all centered on what's happening right inside my own house, with him coming in and messing with my things. Other than that, everything else in my life is completely normal.

There are no hallucinations, no mood episode symptoms (depressive or manic), no disorganized speech or behavior, and no negative symptoms.
